sentences.text: The scientific name Micropachycephalosaurus holds the record for being the longest dinosaur genus name, containing exactly 23 letters.
This small creature likely reached a maximum length of just one meter.
Researchers suggest the animal may have sported striped skin to blend in with surrounding plants.
It lived in the understory, staying very close to the ground.
The holotype specimen IVPP V5542, which is the specific specimen the species is based on, was discovered on a cliff southwest of Laiyang in Shandong Province, China.
Dong Zhiming formally named and described this dinosaur in 1978.
Micropachycephalosaurus was a bipedal herbivore that walked on two legs.
Its diet likely consisted of nibbling on leaves and roots instead of swallowing large amounts of vegetation.
Originally, its non-domed skull, open supratemporal fenestra, and descended quadratojugal led scientists to classify it as a member of the Homalocephalidae.
However, a 2011 cladistic analysis later placed it as a basal member of the Ceratopsia.
Fossil evidence indicates Micropachycephalosaurus lived approximately 77 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
It inhabited China during the Campanian stage of that epoch.
The environment was likely a mix of river and lake systems.
Conversely, the Paleobiology Database records a wider time range from the Coniacian to Santonian stages, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
A 2024 phylogenetic analysis recovered Micropachycephalosaurus as a basal pachycephalosaur, contradicting earlier classifications.
